From: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@bytechain.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-04T16:22:00Z
Subject: Initial pricing questions for hosted API (per-token)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the latency numbers looked promising. Before we commit to a pilot, the finance team asked for a clearer breakdown of how Redwood's per-token discounts stack with model‑specific premiums. A couple quick asks:

- If we commit to a 6mo volume (monthly average ~3B tokens), what discount bands apply to chat vs embeddings?
- Do premium models (larger/latest LLMs) carry a fixed multiplier or an absolute per-token surcharge?
- Is there a blended rate we can use for forecast modeling if our mix is ~70% chat / 30% embeddings?

Can you send a concise table and any standard contract language around commit tiers? We need something short for internal approval.

Best,
Samantha Jones
VP, Platform Partnerships
ByteChain

Attachments: ByteChain_requirements_notes.docx (referenced)

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@bytechain.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-05T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions for hosted API (per-token)

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear list. Short answer: yes, we have tiered per-token discounts and separate model multipliers for premium models; we can also provide a blended pro-forma rate for forecasting.

Quick follow-ups to make the table precise:
- Is the 3B/month an observed steady-state expectation or peak-month planning?
- For embeddings: any expected long vs short vectors (we price per-embed unit but longer vectors can affect cost).
- Do you expect sustained use of our top-tier premium models for chat (e.g., redwood-premium-xxl) or would you accept a fall‑back to a slightly smaller premium variant?

If you prefer, we can sketch two options: a straightforward commit with model premiums applied as multipliers, or a blended commit that guarantees a single effective per-token rate with a model‑usage reconciliation each quarter. I’ve looped in Marissa for deal structure and Aditya for model-premium specifics.

I’ll attach a sample pricing grid and a draft SOW for your team to review.

Thanks — talk soon.

Rachel Kim
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_model_pricing_grid_2026.xlsx, ByteChain_SOW_v1.pdf

On Feb 4, 2026 11:22 AM, Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@bytechain.ai> wrote:
> Hi Rachel,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the latency numbers looked promising...

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-05T10:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Fwd: ByteChain - clarifying commit bands & model premiums

Hey team — draft numbers below (quick, intended for the one‑pager). I’ve left room for a blended calculation and flagged items that need legal/finance language.

Proposal A — Multiplier model (simple, transparent):
- Base hosted per-token (standard chat): $0.0000080 / token (no commit)
- Commit discounts (applied to base chat rate):
  - 0-0.5B/mo: 0%
  - 0.5-1.5B/mo: 10%
  - 1.5-3.0B/mo: 18%
  - >3.0B/mo: 25%
- Premium model multiplier (chat premium models): x1.6 (i.e., multiply the effective chat per-token after discount)
- Embeddings pricing: base $0.0000025 / embed-unit
  - Embeddings premium multiplier (larger embed models): x1.2

Example (their stated mix, 3B tokens/month, 70% chat / 30% embeddings):
- Effective chat base after commit discount at 3B (25%): $0.0000060/token -> premium chat = $0.0000096/token
- Embeds base after commit discount at 3B (25%): $0.000001875/embed -> premium embed = $0.00000225/embed
- Blended sample rate (approx): compute weighted avg across token-equivalent: ~ $0.0000076 per token-equivalent (we'll provide spreadsheet).

Proposal B — Blended commit rate (preferred for forecasting):
- Agree to a single blended per-token rate for the billing period based on forecasted mix (e.g., $0.0000075/token) with quarterly reconciliation if actual model mix skews >10% against forecast.
- Reconciliation: either a small true-up surcharge or credit depending on direction.

Operational notes / asks:
- We should offer a 90‑day rate guarantee for the committed term and standard hosted SLOs (p99 latency SLAs optional at additional fee).
- Embed vs chat unit normalization: finance prefers a per-token-equivalent conversion table — I can add that to the spreadsheet.

Attachments: redwood_model_pricing_grid_2026.xlsx (contains worked examples).

Thoughts? I kept numbers conservative to leave room for slight discounting during legal.

- Aditya

PS: Marissa — for contract language, propose a simple clause: "Committed Usage" defined as the aggregate monthly token units; Billing at blended or multiplier approach as elected; quarterly reconciliation allowed. Legal to draft exact wording.

From: Samantha Jones <samantha.jones@bytechain.ai>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Cc: ByteChain Finance <finance@bytechain.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-09T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: ByteChain - clarifying commit bands & model premiums

Thanks — this is very helpful. The finance team likes Proposal B (single blended rate with reconciliation). A few quick clarifications before we run this up for approval: 

1) Can you provide the blended sample using our exact expected mix and a 6‑month term (we'll use 3B/mo steady-state in the model)?
2) For the blended rate, can Redwood guarantee no surprise model-premium surcharges within the quarter (i.e., we only reconcile after the quarter ends)?
3) Are the p99 latency SLOs part of the hosted package or add-on? If add-on, what's the incremental cost (rough figure)?

If you can send the one‑pager and the updated spreadsheet with the 6‑month blended line and the reconciliation language, we'll put this to procurement next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Samantha
